correctness.rationale: The zero-padding lemma is proved by considering three exhaustive types of deletion positions. At length sixteen, 129 guarded candidate words are enumerated and the exact compatibility graph is searched to completion by a correct coloring-bound clique algorithm, giving maximum fourteen with an attaining explicit code and 33491 visited nodes. A separate 16-word witness at length seventeen has directly verified pairwise disjoint one-deletion shadows. An independent integer-programming formulation reproduces the upper-bound optimum but is not used as an exact proof.

value.rationale: The object is the standard guarded binary (2,infinity) run-length-limited input constraint for synchronization-error correction. Determining the first blocklength for sixteen distinguishable deletion-corrected messages is a natural four-bit engineering/theoretical cutoff rather than an arbitrary indexed slice. The sharp fourteen-word obstruction at sixteen is not supplied by the published nonasymptotic or fractional-matching bounds; a finite complete capacity and a threshold witness are reusable benchmarks. No assertion of a general capacity formula or implementation-level performance is needed.
